language.script_notes: A higher proportion of Aboriginal place names and community signage than the coastal cities.
false_friends: Sub-Saharan Africa (Sahel region — similarly red soil, sparse thorny scrub, flat terrain)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Often minimal or entirely absent on remote highways.
road_furniture.line_paint: Many roads are a single unmarked lane in each direction with wide dirt shoulders.
road_furniture.curb_style: Essentially absent; isolated roadhouses serve as the only 'infrastructure' for long stretches.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Northern Territory utility poles are distinctively metal with holes in them, unlike poles further south and east. The Stuart Highway (Alice Springs to Darwin/Pimba) is a strong geographic anchor — long, straight, orange-dirt roads with sparse short trees.

architecture.roof_style: Simple, utilitarian low buildings; almost no dense urban development outside a handful of towns (Alice Springs, Darwin).
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal roofing, built to withstand extreme heat.
architecture.wall_construction: Isolated roadhouses and simple demountable/prefab buildings are the dominant built form across vast, empty stretches.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Sun-faded, dust-covered tones matching the surrounding red earth.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Isolated roadhouses along long empty highways; almost no continuous urban development; Uluru and other iconic red-rock formations as unmistakable landmarks where visible.

nature.vegetation: Sparse spinifex grass, desert oak and low thorny scrub dominate; vegetation thins dramatically compared to the coastal regions.
nature.terrain: Vast, flat, arid interior dominated by red/orange dirt and sand, including the Simpson Desert; famous red-rock landmarks (Uluru, Kata Tjuta) rise abruptly from the flat desert.
nature.climate_signature: The single strongest Outback tell is the vivid orange-red dirt beside the road, combined with sparse short vegetation and an enormous, empty horizon — hot, dry and intensely sunny.

vehicles.plate_color: Northern Territory plates sometimes show red-tinged text on white.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy-duty 4WD utes and road trains (multi-trailer trucks) are disproportionately common given the vast distances and remote conditions.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Sparse; where present, often older coverage along the handful of major highways (Stuart Highway).
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Huge coverage gaps — Street View exists mainly along the very limited highway network connecting isolated towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Similar red/orange soil, sparse thorny scrub, flat arid terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Australia's Outback combines its red dirt with left-hand traffic, English road signage and eucalyptus/spinifex-specific vegetation; the Sahel has completely different road furniture, often French-influenced signage, and different vegetation species.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Outback is red-dirt, sparsely vegetated and largely empty of buildings; the East Coast is green, densely developed and suburban.
